newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Wall St bulls cheered by broad rally.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Wall St bulls cheered by broad rally.

text.p: Wall Street bulls were cheered on Tuesday by a sharp rally in stocks that spread to broad sectors of the market.

The recent rebound in stocks had seen a handful of large capitalization blue chip stocks leaving their smaller-cap brethern behind, raising concern among technical analysts that the recovery lacked a strong base.
But with advancing stocks outpacing decliners by almost four to one on the New York Stock Exchange on Tuesday, some analysts were saying Wall Street's correction had ended.
"I think basically the correction is over that started seven weeks ago," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons.
The Dow industrials were up 131 points, or 1.9 percent, at 6913 in afternoon trading after market-friendly economic data eased inflation worries.
The Nasdaq composite also took part in the surge, jumping 19 points, or 1.6 percent, to 1236.
Even the battered small-cap gauge Russell 2000 was up over three points, or one percent, to 339.
The Dow could take a breather ahead of a key report on April employment on Friday before making an assault on its record highs, technical analysts said.
The Dow closed at a record of 7085.16 on March 11 then slid to its recent closing low of 6391.69 on April 11.

"I wouldn't be surprised if you get the Dow to new highs, it's really not that far from here," said Ken Tower, technical analyst at UST Securities. But he was less sanguine about smaller stocks, saying they had suffered "too much damage" to be able to mount a major rebound.
"I'd be more suprised if the S&P (500) goes to new highs, and I'd be shocked if something like the Russell 2000 makes it to a new high," Tower said.
The Dow was about three percent off its record closing high.
The S&P was almost four percent off its February 18 high of 816.29. On Tuesday it was up about two percent, gaining 16 points to 787.
Meanwhile, the Russell 2000 was about nine percent off its January 22 closing high of 370.75.

"I would expect a continued choppy market in general, but with the focus on the large caps," said Jonathan Dodd, technical analyst at Dean Witter. "Secondaries may play some catch-up, but that's still a lagging area."
A split market between large cap and small cap stocks over an extended period is normally viewed as a negative for the overall market, the technical analysts said.
